title: Right to Information Act, 2005
ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
summary: Empowers any citizen to request information from a public authority, which must reply within 30 days. Establishes Public Information Officers, the Central and State Information Commissions, and a penalty regime for denial.
body: An Act to provide for setting out the practical regime of right to information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority. Every public authority must designate Public Information Officers. A request must be disposed of within thirty days; where it concerns the life or liberty of a person, within forty-eight hours. Appeals lie to the First Appellate Authority and then the Information Commission.

title: Information Technology Act, 2000
summary: India's primary law on cybercrime and electronic commerce. Gives legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures and defines offences such as hacking, identity theft, and publishing obscene material electronically.
body: An Act to provide legal recognition for transactions carried out by means of electronic data interchange and other means of electronic communication. Sections 43 and 66 deal with unauthorised access and computer-related offences; Section 66C with identity theft; Section 66D with cheating by personation using a computer resource; Section 67 with publishing obscene material in electronic form. The Act was amended in 2008 to add data protection and cyber-terrorism provisions.

title: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
summary: Procedural law governing the investigation, inquiry and trial of criminal offences in India, including arrest, bail, FIR registration, and the powers of police and courts.
body: The Code consolidates the law relating to criminal procedure. Section 154 provides for registration of a First Information Report in cognizable cases; Section 41 governs when police may arrest without warrant; Sections 437 and 439 deal with bail. It has largely been replaced by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, with effect from 1 July 2024.

title: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
summary: The new code of substantive criminal law replacing the Indian Penal Code, 1860 from 1 July 2024. Re-numbers offences and introduces community service and new provisions on organised crime and terrorism.
body: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita repeals the Indian Penal Code. Murder is now Section 103, cheating Section 318, criminal breach of trust Section 316. It adds a definition of organised crime (Section 111) and petty organised crime (Section 112), and introduces community service as a punishment for minor offences.

title: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
summary: The new procedural criminal code replacing the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 from 1 July 2024. Mandates time-bound investigation, e-FIR / Zero FIR, and forensic visits for serious offences.
body: The Sanhita provides for registration of FIR at any police station irrespective of jurisdiction (Zero FIR), electronic filing of information, mandatory videography of search and seizure, and forensic examination of the scene for offences punishable with seven years or more. It sets timelines for filing of charge sheets and pronouncement of judgment.

title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
summary: India's first comprehensive data protection law. Regulates processing of digital personal data, requires consent, creates the Data Protection Board, and provides rights to data principals.
body: The Act applies to processing of digital personal data within India and to processing outside India in connection with offering goods or services to data principals in India. It requires a notice-and-consent framework, imposes obligations on data fiduciaries, gives individuals the right to access, correction and erasure, and establishes the Data Protection Board of India to adjudicate breaches with penalties up to Rs 250 crore.

title: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015)
summary: Landmark judgment striking down Section 66A of the IT Act as unconstitutional for violating the freedom of speech under Article 19(1)(a). A foundational free-speech precedent for the internet in India.
body: The Supreme Court held that Section 66A of the Information Technology Act, 2000, which criminalised sending 'offensive' messages through a computer or communication device, was vague, over-broad and had a chilling effect on free speech. The Court read down Section 79 and the Intermediary Guidelines, holding that intermediaries are required to take down content only on a court order or government notification.

title: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017) — Right to Privacy
summary: A nine-judge bench unanimously held that the right to privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution. The constitutional foundation for India's data-protection regime.
body: The Supreme Court declared that the right to privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 and as a part of the freedoms guaranteed by Part III of the Constitution. The judgment laid down the proportionality test for any state intrusion into privacy and directly informed the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

title: CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011)
summary: Held that examinees have a right under the RTI Act to inspect their evaluated answer scripts. A key precedent on the scope of 'information' and exemptions under the RTI Act.
body: The Supreme Court held that an evaluated answer book is 'information' under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act and that a candidate is entitled to inspect it, subject to the exemptions in Section 8. The Court cautioned against an interpretation that would impose an impractical burden on public authorities.

title: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)
summary: National financial-inclusion mission providing every household a basic bank account with no minimum balance, a RuPay debit card, accident insurance cover, and access to overdraft and pension products.
body: PMJDY ensures access to financial services — banking/savings and deposit accounts, remittance, credit, insurance and pension — in an affordable manner. Account holders receive a RuPay debit card with built-in accident insurance cover and an overdraft facility after satisfactory operation. It is the delivery backbone for Direct Benefit Transfer of government subsidies.

title: Atal Pension Yojana (APY)
summary: Guaranteed pension scheme for workers in the unorganised sector. Subscribers aged 18-40 contribute monthly to receive a fixed pension of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 per month from age 60.
body: Under the Atal Pension Yojana, a subscriber receives a guaranteed minimum monthly pension of Rs 1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000 or 5,000 from the age of 60, depending on the contribution and the age of joining. The same pension is payable to the spouse on the subscriber's death, and the accumulated corpus is returned to the nominee. It is administered by the PFRDA.

title: National Pension System (NPS)
summary: Voluntary, defined-contribution retirement savings scheme open to all citizens aged 18-70, regulated by the PFRDA, with market-linked returns and tax benefits.
body: The National Pension System is a government-sponsored pension scheme allowing systematic savings during a subscriber's working life. Contributions are invested in equity, corporate bonds and government securities through registered pension fund managers. On exit, a portion is available as a lump sum and the balance is used to buy an annuity. Additional tax deduction is available under Section 80CCD(1B).

title: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)
summary: Income-support scheme paying eligible landholding farmer families Rs 6,000 per year in three equal instalments directly into their bank accounts.
body: Under PM-KISAN, all landholding farmer families receive financial benefit of Rs 6,000 per year, payable in three four-monthly instalments of Rs 2,000 each, transferred directly to bank accounts through Direct Benefit Transfer. Eligibility is verified through state land records and Aadhaar seeding.

title: Digital India Programme
summary: Flagship programme to transform India into a digitally empowered society, covering digital infrastructure, governance and services on demand, and digital literacy.
body: Digital India is built on three vision areas: digital infrastructure as a utility to every citizen, governance and services on demand, and digital empowerment of citizens. It includes initiatives such as DigiLocker, UMANG, e-Sign, Common Service Centres, and the BharatNet rural broadband network.

title: CERT-In Directions on Cyber Security Incident Reporting, 2022
summary: Directions under Section 70B(6) of the IT Act requiring service providers, intermediaries and data centres to report specified cyber incidents to CERT-In within six hours and to retain logs for 180 days.
body: The directions mandate that any service provider, intermediary, data centre, body corporate and government organisation report cyber security incidents (such as data breaches, ransomware and unauthorised access) to CERT-In within six hours of noticing them. Entities must synchronise system clocks to NIC/NPL servers, enable logs and maintain them within India for 180 days, and VPN/cloud providers must retain subscriber records for five years.

title: RBI Guidelines on Digital Lending, 2022
summary: RBI circular regulating digital lending apps. Requires that all loan disbursals and repayments flow directly between borrower and regulated entity, with a Key Fact Statement and a cooling-off period.
body: The guidelines provide that all loan disbursals and repayments must be executed only between the bank accounts of the borrower and the regulated entity, without pass-through accounts of lending service providers. Borrowers must be given a standardised Key Fact Statement disclosing the all-inclusive Annual Percentage Rate, a cooling-off period to exit the loan, and a grievance redressal officer. It targets unregulated and predatory loan apps.

title: Gujarat: Digital Seva Setu / Jan Sevak doorstep services
summary: Gujarat Government Resolution operationalising doorstep delivery of government certificates and services through Common Service Centres and the Digital Seva Setu network at the village level.
body: The resolution rolls out delivery of more than fifty citizen services — income certificate, caste certificate, senior-citizen certificate, ration-card services and land records — through village-level Common Service Centres connected over the Gujarat Fibre Grid. Citizens can apply at a nearby centre instead of travelling to taluka or district offices.

title: Gujarat: One Nation One Ration Card implementation
department: Food, Civil Supplies & Consumer Affairs Department
summary: Gujarat resolution implementing portability of ration cards so beneficiaries can draw their subsidised food grain entitlement from any fair-price shop in the state and across India.
body: Under One Nation One Ration Card, National Food Security Act beneficiaries in Gujarat can lift their entitled quota of food grains from any ePoS-enabled fair-price shop through biometric authentication, regardless of the shop where the card is registered. This supports migrant workers who move within and outside the state.

title: Gujarat: Vahali Dikri Yojana
summary: Gujarat welfare scheme giving financial assistance to families for the first two girl children — instalments at class 1, class 9, and Rs 1,00,000 on attaining adulthood — to promote girls' education and check female foeticide.
body: The Vahali Dikri Yojana provides Rs 4,000 when the girl enters Class 1, Rs 6,000 in Class 9, and Rs 1,00,000 when she turns 18 for higher education or marriage. It applies to the first two daughters of families with an annual income up to Rs 2 lakh, aiming to improve the child sex ratio and the educational status of girls.

title: Gujarat: Namo e-Tablet Yojana
summary: Gujarat scheme providing subsidised tablets to college and polytechnic students enrolled in the first year, to bridge the digital divide in higher education.
body: Under the Namo e-Tablet Yojana, students admitted to the first year of a college or polytechnic course receive a tablet at a nominal subsidised price. The tablet is preloaded with educational content to support digital learning among students from economically weaker families.

title: Cyber Crime Helpline 1930 and National Cybercrime Reporting Portal
summary: National toll-free helpline 1930 and the cybercrime.gov.in portal for reporting financial cyber fraud, enabling rapid freezing of defrauded funds through the Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System.
body: Citizens who fall victim to online financial fraud can call the toll-free number 1930 or report on cybercrime.gov.in. The Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System connects banks, wallets and payment aggregators so that fraudulent transactions can be flagged and the money held before it is withdrawn by the fraudster. The portal also handles complaints relating to women and child safety.

title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
summary: Modernised consumer law establishing the Central Consumer Protection Authority, rules for e-commerce and misleading advertisements, product liability, and easier online filing of complaints.
body: The Act replaces the Consumer Protection Act, 1986. It sets up the Central Consumer Protection Authority to regulate matters relating to violation of consumer rights, unfair trade practices and misleading advertisements. It introduces product liability, provides for filing complaints electronically and from the consumer's place of residence, and brings e-commerce and direct selling within its ambit.

title: IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021
summary: Rules under the IT Act requiring social-media intermediaries to appoint grievance, compliance and nodal officers, enable traceability of message originators, and follow a code of ethics for digital news and OTT platforms.
body: The Rules impose due-diligence obligations on intermediaries, including a grievance redressal mechanism with defined timelines. Significant social-media intermediaries must appoint a Chief Compliance Officer, a Nodal Contact Person and a Resident Grievance Officer, publish monthly compliance reports, and enable identification of the first originator of information. A three-tier grievance mechanism governs digital news publishers and OTT platforms.

title: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY)
summary: World's largest government-funded health-assurance scheme, providing eligible families a cover of Rs 5 lakh per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation, cashless and paperless at empanelled hospitals.
body: PM-JAY provides health cover of Rs 5,00,000 per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation to economically vulnerable families identified through the Socio-Economic Caste Census. Treatment is cashless and paperless at any empanelled public or private hospital across India, with no cap on family size or age.

title: Mandatory Linking of Aadhaar with PAN
summary: CBDT notification under Section 139AA of the Income-tax Act requiring every person allotted a PAN to link it with Aadhaar, failing which the PAN becomes inoperative.
body: Under Section 139AA of the Income-tax Act, 1961, every person who has been allotted a Permanent Account Number and is eligible to obtain an Aadhaar number must intimate the Aadhaar to the prescribed authority. A PAN not linked with Aadhaar by the notified deadline becomes inoperative, affecting filing of returns, refunds and high-value transactions.
